Notifications — the bell and the notifications page

The top-bar bell and the Notifications page — where SATOM tells you that a backup, job, scan or bug report you care about has finished, failed or needs attention.

👤 ForViewerOperatorAdministrator
📍 WhereTop bar → bell icon · View all notifications (URL /notifications)
On this page
  • What is it?
  • What does it do?

What is it?#

The bell in the top bar is SATOM's personal inbox. Background work you started — a backup, a firmware transfer, a hardware scan — and events addressed to you, such as an alert or a resolved bug report, arrive here as notifications. Each one belongs to one user, has a read/unread state and survives restarts.

What does it do?#

  • Shows a red counter of unread notifications on the bell, refreshed every 30 seconds without reloading the page.
  • Opens a drop-down with the 8 most recent notifications (title and time).
  • Lists up to the 100 most recent on the Notifications page, with the description and a link to the related page when there is one.
  • Uses four kinds, each with its own icon and colour: information (blue), success (green), warning (amber) and error (red).

Typical notifications:

Title (examples) Raised when
Backup ready: fweb-01 / Backup failed: fweb-01 A backup you started finishes.
Firmware image ready: … / Firmware upload failed A firmware upload you started finishes.
Hardware scan: N scanned, M failed A hardware scan you started failed on one or more devices (a fully successful scan does not notify).
sweep failed: … A monitoring probe sweep you started fails.
New bug report: </em></td> <td>Someone used <strong>Report a problem</strong> (administrators).</td> </tr> <tr> <td><em>Your bug report was resolved</em></td> <td>An administrator resolved your report.</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Alert titles</td> <td>The alert engine finds a problem (administrators; also by email if configured).</td> </tr> </tbody> </table></div> <p>Device actions (upgrades, reboots and similar), signature syncs and release-note scans also notify the user who started them.</p> <h2 id="requirements">Requirements<a class="dc-anchor" href="#requirements" title="Permanent link">#</a></h2> <p>None — every signed-in user has a bell.</p> <h2 id="permissions">Permissions<a class="dc-anchor" href="#permissions" title="Permanent link">#</a></h2> <p>No permission is needed. You only ever see <strong>your own</strong> notifications. Alert and new-bug-report notifications are sent to every active administrator (<a class="dc-perm" href="permissions.html#users-manage" title="Manage users — Create, edit, delete, reset and re-profile users"><code>users.manage</code></a>).</p> <h2 id="how-to-use">How to use<a class="dc-anchor" href="#how-to-use" title="Permanent link">#</a></h2> <h3 id="check-the-bell">Check the bell<a class="dc-anchor" href="#check-the-bell" title="Permanent link">#</a></h3> <ol> <li>A filled bell with a number means unread notifications.</li> <li>Click the bell to open the drop-down. Click an entry to open its page.</li> <li>Click <strong>Clear</strong> to mark them all as read. The badge disappears, but the notifications stay on the Notifications page.</li> </ol> <h3 id="open-the-full-list">Open the full list<a class="dc-anchor" href="#open-the-full-list" title="Permanent link">#</a></h3> <ol> <li>In the drop-down click <strong>View all notifications ›</strong>.</li> <li>The page <strong>Notifications</strong> lists them newest first. Entries that were unread are highlighted with a dot for this visit.</li> <li>Opening the page marks everything as read.</li> </ol> <h3 id="delete-your-notifications">Delete your notifications<a class="dc-anchor" href="#delete-your-notifications" title="Permanent link">#</a></h3> <ol> <li>Open the <strong>Notifications</strong> page (bell → <strong>View all notifications ›</strong>).</li> <li>Click <strong>Clear all</strong> at the top right. The button is shown only when the list is not empty.</li> <li>Confirm <em>"Delete all your notifications? This cannot be undone."</em>. The page reloads with <em>"Notifications cleared."</em>.</li> </ol> <p><strong>Clear all</strong> deletes your notifications of the current ADOM (in a product ADOM its own notifications — FortiWeb also unscoped ones; in <strong>Global</strong> all of them). It never touches other users' notifications.</p> <div class="dc-co dc-co-note"> <p class="dc-co-title"><span class="dc-co-ico">ℹ️</span>Note</p> <p><strong>Changed in 2.11.0:</strong> the Notifications page has a <strong>Clear all</strong> button that deletes your notifications of the current ADOM; before, notifications could only be marked as read.</p> </div> <h2 id="configuration">Configuration<a class="dc-anchor" href="#configuration" title="Permanent link">#</a></h2> <p>Nothing to configure for the bell. Email delivery of alerts is set up by an administrator in <strong>Settings → Monitoring & Alerts → Email & Alerts</strong> (see <a href="alerting.html">Alerting</a>).</p> <h2 id="result">Result<a class="dc-anchor" href="#result" title="Permanent link">#</a></h2> <p><strong>Clear</strong> in the bell and opening the page only change the read state; nothing is deleted. <strong>Clear all</strong> on the Notifications page deletes the notifications of the current ADOM permanently.</p> <h2 id="troubleshooting">Troubleshooting<a class="dc-anchor" href="#troubleshooting" title="Permanent link">#</a></h2> <h3 id="the-bell-shows-nothing-although-a-job-finished">The bell shows nothing although a job finished<a class="dc-anchor" href="#the-bell-shows-nothing-although-a-job-finished" title="Permanent link">#</a></h3> <p><strong>Possible causes</strong> - You are in a different ADOM. Notifications are scoped like everything else: a product ADOM shows its own notifications (FortiWeb also shows unscoped ones); <strong>Global</strong> shows all of them. - The job was started by another user — notifications go to the person who started the work.</p> <p><strong>Solution</strong> — switch to the Global ADOM and open the bell again; check the <strong>Jobs</strong> page for other users' work (administrators see every job).</p> <h3 id="the-counter-does-not-go-down">The counter does not go down<a class="dc-anchor" href="#the-counter-does-not-go-down" title="Permanent link">#</a></h3> <p><strong>Possible causes</strong> — the badge is refreshed every 30 seconds.</p> <p><strong>Solution</strong> — click <strong>Clear</strong>, or open <strong>View all notifications ›</strong>; both mark the notifications of the current ADOM as read immediately.</p> <h3 id="youre-all-caught-up-no-notifications">"You're all caught up — no notifications."<a class="dc-anchor" href="#youre-all-caught-up-no-notifications" title="Permanent link">#</a></h3> <p>There is nothing in your inbox for the current ADOM. Switch to Global to see notifications from every product.</p> <h2 id="advanced">Advanced<a class="dc-anchor" href="#advanced" title="Permanent link">#</a></h2> <details class="dc-adv"> <summary><span class="dc-adv-tag">Advanced</span> Storage and scoping</summary> <ul> <li>Notifications are rows in PostgreSQL (<code>notifications</code> table) with the recipient, kind, title (up to 200 characters), optional body and link, read flag, creation time and the ADOM they were raised in.</li> <li>Writing a notification never makes the triggering operation fail; a failure to notify is only logged.</li> <li>Notifications raised by background workers (for example the alert engine) carry the appliance's ADOM when they concern a device, otherwise they are unscoped.</li> <li><strong>Clear all</strong> posts to <code>/notifications/clear</code> (CSRF-protected) and deletes the rows of the current ADOM scope; the bell's <strong>Clear</strong> posts to <code>/notifications/dismiss</code> and only marks them read.</li> </ul> </details></article> <div class="dc-tags"><a class="dc-tag" href="search.html?q=notifications">#notifications</a><a class="dc-tag"
